title: DevKit presets and local-sim runbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a lightweight developer kit (DevKit) that lets engineers run Redwood-like inference flows locally without GPUs by using small reference presets and a local-sim runtime. Goal is to shorten the time-to-first-success for SDK adopters and surface common failure modes before they hit hosted/Dedicated environments.

Audience:
- Product engineers and SDK integrators who want to prototype fast
- Solutions engineers who need reproducible demos
- New joiners doing first SDK experiments

Scope and constraints (what this doc is *not*):
- Not a production deployment guide for Dedicated/Private
- Not intended for benchmarking accurate latency/cost numbers
- Should run on macOS/Linux developer laptops, WSL; optional Docker image for parity

Key ideas and differentiators vs existing quickstarts:
- Preset profiles (tiny, dev, smoke) that are application-oriented (chat, embeddings, rerank) rather than only model-focused
- Local-sim runtime: emulates token streams, KV caching behavior and simulates batching delays so developer code sees realistic pacing and failure patterns without a GPU
- CLI-first flow with a tiny web-based inspector for requests/responses
- Offramp patterns: one-command uplift to hosted API or Dedicated (copy config, swap credentials)

High-level components:
- devkit CLI (devkit local up, devkit preset apply, devkit run sample)
- local-sim server (node/python microservice) that implements subset of Redwood API surface for text/chat/embeddings
- presets: JSON files that declare model family, quantization level (sim), token-cost multipliers, latency profile, example evals
- sample apps: minimal chat, serverless function adapter, embeddings indexer
- diagnostics inspector: lightweight web UI to view streams, KV cache state, and simulated batching

Preset profiles (initial proposals):
- tiny: "tiny-chat" — 16-token context limit, immediate token streaming, cost multiplier 0.01. For smoke tests and offline demos.
- dev: "dev-chat" — 512-token context, simulated 20ms token latency, simple prefix caching enabled. For normal developer iteration.
- serverlike: "dev-embed" — embedding vector dim tuned down, batch simulation to show throughput backpressure. Good for integrating embedding pipelines.
- failure-mode: "unstable" — randomized 5-10% dropped requests, token truncation tests, to exercise retry/fallback logic.

Example preset JSON (illustrative, stored under devkit/presets):

{
  "name": "dev-chat",
  "model_family": "ref-small",
  "context_limit": "512",
  "latency_profile_ms": "20",
  "cost_multiplier": "0.05",
  "kv_caching": "prefix"
}

(Local files will be simplified — keep editable so SEs can tweak)

Local-sim runtime behavior (what to emulate):
- Streaming: send tokens at configured token-intervals to exercise client streaming handlers
- KV cache hooks: expose endpoints to inspect stored prefixes and cache hits/misses
- Batching: when run in batch mode, accumulate requests per small time-window to trigger server-side batching logic in user code (simulate SLO vs throughput tradeoffs)
- Error injection: toggles for transient errors, rate-limit responses, corrupted JSON output

Developer flows (CLI):
1) First-run: devkit local up --preset dev-chat
   - spins local-sim server on 127.0.0.1:1823
   - prints example env exports: REDWOOD_LOCAL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1823
   - opens inspector at http://127.0.0.1:1824
2) Run sample chat: devkit run sample chat --prompt \"Summarize last meeting\"
3) Switch to hosted: devkit preset apply hosted-demo --copy-credentials
   - outputs diff of config changes required for hosted endpoints

Runbook: common checklist for onboarding new team members or customers
- [ ] Install: node 18+ OR docker, pip deps (if python runtime)
- [ ] devkit local up --preset dev-chat (confirm inspector reachable)
- [ ] Run sample: devkit run sample chat (observe streaming tokens)
- [ ] Force failure: devkit local fault inject --drop 10 (verify client retries)
- [ ] Test lift: devkit preset apply hosted-demo (verify app works with hosted creds)

Sample quickstart readme (2-minute flow):
1. git clone github.com/redwood-inference/devkit
2. cd devkit && npm ci (or pip install -r requirements.txt)
3. devkit local up --preset tiny-chat
4. export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1823 && node examples/chat.js
5. Open inspector to see token stream and KV cache hits

Integration notes for SDKs (areas to add in docs):
- How to configure SDK to use local endpoint (env var map, config file example)
- Examples for streaming handlers in JS/Python/Go (small snippets for token callback)
- Error handling patterns: retry backoff, idempotency keys for batch endpoints, graceful fallback to smaller model presets

Diagnostics and observability guidance:
- DevKit inspector shows: request timeline, simulated queue depth, token emission histogram, KV cache hit rates per prefix
- Logging: structured JSON lines (ts, req_id, preset, latency_ms, error_code) to make grep/rg debugging consistent

Onboarding checklist for documentation pages (product docs):
- Short one-page overview: what DevKit is for, TL;DR commands
- Presets gallery: table with presets and recommended use cases
- Troubleshooting appendix: common errors, how to increase context window in preset, how to reduce simulated latency
- Migration path section: one-command uplift to hosted (explain credential swap, config differences)

Open questions / TODOs (urgent):
- Which subset of Redwood API surface do we mimic? minimal: text/generate, chat/stream, embeddings. Do we also include tool-calling stub endpoints? (TODO: discuss with product)
- Desktop-friendly UI: do we maintain React inspector or an electron wrapper? MVP: web inspector only.
- Should presets be versioned and published like model catalog entries? How do we map to hosted model ids?
- Ownership: who will maintain presets long-term (eng-developer-experience vs solutions-engineering)?

Milestones (rough):
- Week 0-2: prototype local-sim server + 3 presets + CLI up/down commands
- Week 3-4: sample apps (chat, embed), inspector basic view, docs page drafts
- Week 5-6: integration tests for SDKs (JS/Python), demo scripts for SEs
- Week 7: beta release to internal teams and select external partners

Notes to self / meeting fragments:
- 2025-11-03: Liam suggested adding a \"latency noise\" toggle to simulate network jitter — good for streaming edge cases
- 2025-11-10: Sofia demoed a serverless adapter that translates local requests into an event format; keep that sample in examples/adapter

Quick command summary (MVP):
- devkit local up --preset <name>
- devkit local down
- devkit run sample <chat|embed|rerank> --prompt \"...\"
- devkit preset list
- devkit fault inject --type drop --pct 5

Appendix: example SDK config snippet for local testing (env var example)

# bash
export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1823
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=local-test-key

Problems to watch for during beta:
- Preset semantics confusion: keep names explicit (e.g., dev-embed-small) rather than ambiguous shorthand
- Too many knobs in CLI -> keep MVP to 6 key commands
- Platform parity: make it *easy* to swap a single env var to go from local to hosted

Next actions (this week):
- Asha: spin up initial local-sim repo skeleton and prototype token streaming (ETA 3 days)
- Liam: prepare a sample chat adapter in examples/ with JS and Python (ETA 5 days)
- Sofia: design inspector wireframe and minimal API to expose KV/cache state (ETA 1 week)
- Create GH project: devkit/local-sim and link to JIRA DE-314 (owner: Asha)

Contact: reach out in #dev-experience on Slack for sync; leave notes and blockers in the GH project.

(End of sketch — intended for team editing; keep this doc as a living artifact while we iterate on the MVP)
